title: NY State Assembly · District 43
area: Central Brooklyn: Crown Heights, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, and Flatbush

context.text: Incumbent Brian A. Cunningham (D, WFP) defeated Ahron Gluck 80.8%–18.5% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. The Republican primary was canceled, and Anna Shpilkovskaya advanced from the Republican primary without appearing on the ballot; she also holds the Community First Party line. The Working Families Party primary was also canceled, with Cunningham advancing unopposed.

candidates.name: Brian A. Cunningham
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 80.8% of the vote

summary.text: Brian A. Cunningham is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent in Assembly District 43, representing Crown Heights, Prospect Lefferts Gardens, and Flatbush since a March 2022 special election. He is seeking re-election to a third full term and won his June 2026 Democratic primary with 80.8% of the vote.

background.text: Born and raised in New York City to Jamaican immigrant parents in a working-class family.

Before the Assembly, he served as Chief of Staff in the New York City Council and as a Special Assistant in the New York State Senate, and was the first person elected to run a Cure Violence site in New York City, working to reduce gun violence in Central Brooklyn.
He worked as a youth advisor with organizations including CAMBA and NPower, and as an aide to President Obama's My Brother's Keeper Alliance.

He currently serves as First Vice Chair of the New York State Association of Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislators, Inc., and was the inaugural Treasurer of the New York State Black Legislative Task Force.

priorities.text: Housing: has championed legislation to expand faith-based affordable housing, combat deed theft, and address bad-faith landlord practices.
Education: has advanced the High Impact Tutoring Act and the Caribbean Steel Pan Educational Music Program Act to expand opportunities for New York's youth.

Public safety and mental health: has sponsored measures to expand youth mobile crisis outreach and supports alternatives to violence, including the annual Central Brooklyn Classic basketball tournament.

positions.summary: Prime sponsor of the Faith-Based Affordable Housing Act (A3647-B), which would require towns, villages, and cities to allow denser residential construction on land owned by religious institutions, with at least 20% of units set aside as affordable for most of the state.

Sponsor of a bill (A2666) requiring all municipal corporations statewide to adopt Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE) and Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE) programs within one year.

record.text: Prime sponsor of the Faith-Based Affordable Housing Act (A3647-B); as of the 2025-2026 session the bill has been amended and remains in the Assembly Local Governments Committee.

Prime sponsor of the High Impact Tutoring Act (A2625-A), establishing a pilot grant program for local education providers to implement high-impact tutoring for low-income or underserved students; amended and recommitted to the Education Committee in April 2026.

Prime sponsor of the New York City Caribbean Steel Pan Educational Music Program Act (A00194), which would let NYC community school boards authorize school-grounds use in summer for steel pan practice ahead of the Labor Day Parade (West Indian Carnival); remains in the Education Committee.
Sponsor of legislation (A2666) requiring all municipal corporations to adopt SCRIE and DRIE senior/disability rent increase exemption programs.
Serves on the Assembly Agriculture, Banks, Codes, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Economic Development/Job Creation/Commerce and Industry, and Transportation Committees for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves as First Vice Chair of the New York State Association of Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislators, Inc.

candidates.name: Anna Shpilkovskaya
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the canceled Republican primary without appearing on the ballot

summary.text: Anna Shpilkovskaya is the Republican candidate challenging incumbent Brian A. Cunningham in Assembly District 43. She has not held elected office.

background.text: Shpilkovskaya is a board member of the Community First Republican Club, a Brooklyn Republican club active in southern-Brooklyn Assembly and citywide races.

candidates.researchNotes: Shpilkovskaya has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website was found (checked https://ballotpedia.org/Anna_Shpilkovskaya). The only independently verified public statement located is a February 2026 Brooklyn Eagle item in which she, as a Community First Republican Club board member, described the club's endorsements in other races; it does not address her own Assembly District 43 candidacy or any of the 15 issue statements, so no priorities or positions could be documented.

sources.title: Community First Republican Club endorses candidates during its monthly meeting
